## see STAT 545 Lecture 7 webpage for full reference
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

In order to join two tables, they need to have a variable (column) that gives each observation a unique identifier value, and it needs to be the same for both tables.
e.g:
```{r}
# First tibble
df1 <- tibble(ID = 1:3,                     
              Name = c("Sophie", "Josh","Alex"))

# Second tibble
df2 <- tibble(ID = 2:4,                      
              Age = c(20,50,31))
#left_join() joins only the rows in df2 that have a matching ID in df1, and vis-versa for right_join
#inner_join keeps only rows present in both tables
#full_join() keeps all values
left_join(df1, df2, by = "ID")
```

### by=" " MUST be included!!

Use piping operator (%>%) to layer multiple join functions (join more than 2 tables)
